observations.subject: DEF-001 and DEF-002 remediation: developer suites plus real-browser Playwright validation on branch codex/supplier-defect-001-002
observations.source_ref: Test-first remediation on 2026-09-16. Both defects were independently re-verified against source before any change, and three new/updated tests were confirmed RED before the fix and GREEN after. Developer suites on the fixed source: npm run lint exit 0; npm run build --workspace client exit 0; supplier-phase-001-server JUnit 159 testcases / 0 failures / 0 skipped against authorized test-only erp_dev with DB_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 (was 157; two tests added, still above min_tests=157); supplier-phase-001-client JUnit 40 / 0 / 0. Playwright CLI browser validation against a server and client dev server started from this worktree on 127.0.0.1:3000 and 127.0.0.1:5273, logged in as synthetic system-admin pw_def_0916 with approved device binding 4499. DEF-001: creating supplier DEF-0916-095339 showed exactly four completeness warnings and no BANK_ACCOUNT_MISSING; adding an ordering address, an orders primary contact and an HK identifier through the real UI cleared them one by one down to a single PAYMENT_TERM_MISSING, proving the banner is now reachable to zero. Both GET /suppliers/:id and GET /suppliers/:id/completeness returned issues [] and exactly one PAYMENT_TERM_MISSING warning. The residual payment-term warning cannot be cleared in this environment because Business Master has zero Active Payment Terms seeded; payment term is optional by design, so this is an environment data gap, not a Supplier defect. DEF-002: supplier 404 was suspended through the real UI (version 1 -> 2), a second contact was then created through the UI so that a supplier.contact.create audit row became the newest supplier.% row, and replaying POST /suppliers/404/suspend with the original stale version 1 returned 200 with status suspended and version still 2 — the designed §476 idempotent replay. Before the fix this exact sequence returned 409 STATUS_TRANSITION_INVALID, which the new unit test pins. The negative path is intact: POST /suppliers/404/restore on a suspended supplier still returned 409 STATUS_TRANSITION_INVALID. Final reloaded detail page reported 0 console errors and 0 warnings; the only network requests were user/me, the supplier and completeness reads, all 200. Verified at desktop width and at 375x812. Screenshots captured to the session scratchpad (not repository evidence). REV-006 secondary claim REJECTED: the reviewer also asked for assertExpectedVersion to run before the replay return. Design §476 and §1387 specify that a repeated status command already in the same target state returns current state, and a genuine replay necessarily carries a stale version, so that change would break designed idempotency and the pre-existing test at supplierLifecycleService.test.js:85. Not applied.

observations.subject: REV-007 MEDIUM resolution: real-SQL regression coverage for DEF-002 proven to discriminate
observations.source_ref: REV-007 demonstrated that the DEF-002 unit test could not detect the defect it was written for: its fake derives the filter from the implementation own bound params and never inspects the SQL, so a broken hybrid LIKE-OR-IN implementation passed 8/8. The author reproduced that experiment and confirmed it. supplierManagement.integration.test.js now inserts a supplier.contact.create audit row via pool.query between the activate and its replay. Discrimination proven by running both implementations: correct IN(...) gives integration 5/5 pass and unit 8/8 pass; the broken LIKE-OR-IN hybrid gives integration 1 FAILURE and unit 8/8 pass. The broken implementation was applied only transiently and restored with git checkout; grep confirms no LIKE remains. Full re-run after the change: npm run lint exit 0 and supplier-phase-001-server 159 testcases / 0 failures / 0 skipped. The remediation doc claim that the unit fake exercised the filtering was wrong and is corrected in 04_rev_007_independent_review.md.
